slots.practicalActivity: Write a Foundry test file for a simple Vault.sol (deposit/withdraw) covering only happy-path cases, then deliberately try boundary inputs (0, the exact balance, more than the balance) by hand to find the first case that breaks it.
slots.deliverable: A list of at least three specific boundary/edge cases documented as failing tests on your Vault contract.

slots.practicalActivity: Convert the hand-picked boundary tests into a real Foundry fuzz test (`testFuzz_Deposit(uint256 amount)`) using `bound()` to constrain the input, run `forge test`, and confirm all 256 default runs pass.
slots.deliverable: A passing fuzz test function in your Vault test suite, with `bound()`-constrained inputs.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a `VaultHandler` contract with a ghost variable tracking cumulative deposits, wire `targetContract()` to the handler, and write an `invariant_SolvencyCheck` asserting the vault's balance never falls below total deposits across a long, random call sequence.
slots.deliverable: A passing invariant test with a handler contract and ghost variable for your Vault project.

slots.practicalActivity: Run `forge test --fork-url <RPC> --fork-block-number <N>` against a real, pinned mainnet block, reading a real token balance (e.g. a known USDC whale address) to confirm your test is actually seeing live chain state.
slots.deliverable: A fork test pinned to a specific real mainnet block number, reading one real on-chain balance.

slots.practicalActivity: Run `forge snapshot` on your Vault test suite to create `.gas-snapshot`, then introduce a deliberate inefficiency (an extra SLOAD) and run `forge snapshot --check` to watch it fail before reverting the change.
slots.deliverable: A `.gas-snapshot` file plus a log showing `--check` failing on an intentional gas regression, then passing again.

lessons.title: Test Coverage — & What It Doesn't Tell You

slots.practicalActivity: Run `forge coverage --report summary` on your Vault project, find a function under 100%, then write one new test calling it from an unauthorized address to show that 100% coverage alone wouldn't have caught a missing access check.
slots.deliverable: A coverage report plus one new access-control test demonstrating coverage's real blind spot.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: assemble a single test suite for your Vault project combining this chapter's happy-path, fuzz, invariant, fork, and gas-snapshot tests into one cohesive `Vault.t.sol` + `VaultInvariant.t.sol`, and run the complete suite end to end with `forge test -vvv`.
slots.deliverable: A complete, passing multi-layer Vault test suite combining all five testing disciplines from this chapter.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: generate an LCOV coverage report (`forge coverage --report lcov --report-file lcov.info`) for your full Vault suite and write a one-page 'testing strategy' README summarizing which specific risk each layer (fuzz, invariant, fork, gas, coverage) actually covers.
slots.deliverable: An LCOV report plus a one-page written testing-strategy README for the Vault project.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a short comparison note contrasting how you'd fix a bug in a typical web app (hotfix + redeploy) versus how you'd have to handle the same class of bug in your already-deployed Vault contract, using this lesson's immutability framing.
slots.deliverable: A written comparison note on web-app vs. smart-contract bug-fix response.

slots.practicalActivity: Push your Vault project to a real GitHub repo and add the lesson's exact `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (checkout with submodules, foundry-toolchain, `forge fmt --check`, `forge build --sizes`, `forge test -vvv`), then confirm a green run in the Actions tab.
slots.deliverable: A real GitHub Actions workflow run, passing, visible in your repo's Actions tab.

slots.practicalActivity: Add Solhint to the project with a `.solhint.json` extending `solhint:recommended`, run it locally to find and fix at least one real style/security warning, then add a `lint` job to your CI workflow that the `test` job depends on via `needs: lint`.
slots.deliverable: An updated CI workflow with a separate, gating lint job, plus the fixed Solhint warning.

slots.practicalActivity: Run `slither .` locally against your Vault contract, read the actual finding output, then wire `crytic/slither-action` into your CI workflow with `fail-on: high`.
slots.deliverable: A Slither CI job added to the workflow, plus notes on one real finding (or a confirmed clean scan) from your own contract.

lessons.title: Gating Merges on Test & Audit Results

slots.practicalActivity: In your GitHub repo's Settings → Branches, create a branch protection rule on `main` requiring the lint, test, and Slither checks plus one approving review, then open a test PR with a deliberately failing test to confirm the merge button is actually blocked.
slots.deliverable: A screenshot of a blocked 'Merging is blocked' PR, proving the branch protection rule is enforced.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: audit your own CI pipeline end to end — trigger one deliberate failure in each gate (a failing test, a Slither-flagged pattern, an unapproved PR) one at a time, and document in writing that each one actually blocks the merge as designed.
slots.deliverable: A written verification log confirming each of your three CI gates independently blocks a merge.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: time your full CI pipeline run (lint → test → Slither) in GitHub Actions, then reorder jobs or add caching to shave at least 20% off the total wall-clock time, documenting the before/after durations.
slots.deliverable: Before/after CI run-time numbers showing a measured pipeline speedup.

slots.practicalActivity: Get Sepolia testnet ETH from a public faucet, then write a one-page note listing exactly which of your Vault's properties a successful Sepolia deployment would prove versus what it explicitly would not prove about mainnet economic safety.
slots.deliverable: A funded Sepolia test account plus a written mechanics-vs-economics note.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a real `script/Deploy.s.sol` for your Vault contract, first running it unflagged to simulate, then set up a Foundry keystore `--account` and broadcast the real deployment to Sepolia via a named `[rpc_endpoints]` alias.
slots.deliverable: A Vault contract actually deployed to Sepolia via a reviewable, version-controlled deploy script.

slots.practicalActivity: Run `forge verify-contract` against your Sepolia-deployed Vault with correctly ABI-encoded constructor args (`cast abi-encode`), then open the contract on Sepolia Etherscan and confirm the Read/Write Contract tabs are now live.
slots.deliverable: A verified contract on Sepolia Etherscan showing matched source, ABI, and working Read/Write tabs.

slots.practicalActivity: Rewrite your Vault as an upgradeable UUPS contract (`Initializable`, `OwnableUpgradeable`, `UUPSUpgradeable`, an `initialize()` function, and a protected `_authorizeUpgrade`), deploy both the implementation and a proxy pointing at it locally, and confirm calls through the proxy work.
slots.deliverable: A working UUPS proxy + implementation pair for your Vault, deployed and callable locally.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a real testnet Safe (Safe{Wallet}) with at least three owners and a 2-of-3 threshold, propose your Vault's deploy or upgrade transaction to it, and collect the required confirmations before it executes.
slots.deliverable: A real Sepolia Safe multisig with a proposed-and-executed transaction, documented from the Safe{Wallet} queue.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a `strategy.matrix` job to your CI workflow deploying the Vault to at least two testnets (e.g. Sepolia and Base Sepolia) in parallel, and use `CREATE2` with a fixed salt to confirm both deployments land at the identical address.
slots.deliverable: A matrix-deployed Vault live on two different testnets at the identical CREATE2-derived address.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: walk your Vault project through the full Chapter 3 pipeline end to end on a fresh testnet — simulate, broadcast through a Safe-proposed transaction, verify on the explorer, and confirm it's reachable at its predicted CREATE2 address.
slots.deliverable: A single documented run-through showing deploy → multisig-confirm → verify → address-check, all on live testnet infrastructure.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: write a one-page deployment runbook for your own Vault project, specific to its actual constructor arguments, RPC aliases, and Safe signer addresses, that a teammate could follow without asking you anything.
slots.deliverable: A project-specific, standalone deployment runbook document.

lessons.title: Hosting a Frontend for a dApp

slots.practicalActivity: Build a minimal frontend (even a single page with a 'Connect Wallet' button and your Vault's address) and deploy it to Vercel or Netlify, opening a pull request to confirm a real preview-URL deployment is generated automatically.
slots.deliverable: A live hosted frontend URL plus a working PR preview deployment.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a minimal Dockerfile for a small Node.js service (even a stub that just logs new blocks) using a pinned `node:20-slim` base image, `npm ci`, and a non-root user, then run it locally with Docker Desktop and confirm it shows up in the Containers view.
slots.deliverable: A running, non-root containerized service visible in Docker Desktop, built from a pinned base image.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a real `.env.example` for your Vault project listing every variable it needs (RPC_URL, DEPLOYER_PRIVATE_KEY, etc.) with no real values, commit it, then move your actual deploy secrets into GitHub Actions' encrypted secrets store and reference them by name in your CI workflow.
slots.deliverable: A committed `.env.example` plus a CI workflow referencing real secrets only via `${{ secrets.* }}`, never hardcoded.

lessons.title: Choosing RPC & Infra Providers for Production

slots.practicalActivity: Sign up for two free-tier RPC providers (e.g. Alchemy and Infura), configure an `ethers.FallbackProvider` in a small script pointing at both, and test that it still returns a result after you deliberately point the primary at an invalid URL.
slots.deliverable: A working fallback-provider script proving automatic failover between two real RPC providers.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: stand up your Vault project's full off-chain stack together — hosted frontend, containerized stub indexer, `.env.example` committed, secrets in CI, and a fallback RPC config — and write a short architecture diagram showing how the pieces connect.
slots.deliverable: A working, connected off-chain stack plus a one-page architecture diagram.

slots.practicalActivity: Open a real live protocol in a monitoring dashboard (e.g. a public Aave reserve or a Uniswap pool via Tenderly) and record its current utilization, TVL trend, and recent transaction pattern, deciding which of the four numbers you'd watch first for that specific protocol type.
slots.deliverable: Written notes recording one real protocol's actual current health numbers.

slots.practicalActivity: In a monitoring platform's free tier, configure one real alert rule on your deployed Vault contract (e.g. a Transaction Value or Function Call trigger) and verify it actually fires by triggering the condition yourself on testnet.
slots.deliverable: One working, verified alert rule on your own deployed contract, with a confirmed test firing.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a `pause()`/`unpause()` modifier set to your Vault contract, controlled by the Safe multisig from Chapter 3, and rehearse pulling it — propose, confirm, and execute a real pause transaction on testnet.
slots.deliverable: A tested, multisig-gated pause mechanism, actually exercised once on testnet.

slots.practicalActivity: Using your alert history from the previous lesson's test firing, write a full postmortem for that simulated incident following the Summary/Timeline/Impact/Root Cause/What Went Well/What Didn't/Remediation Items skeleton, with a named owner and due date per remediation item.
slots.deliverable: A complete written postmortem document for your simulated incident, following the real skeleton.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: run a full tabletop incident-response drill on your Vault project — simulate an alert firing, pause via the multisig, draft the first-hour public acknowledgment message, and produce the postmortem, timing how long the whole sequence takes.
slots.deliverable: A timed, end-to-end incident-response drill record (acknowledgment message + pause transaction + postmortem).

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: review your alert rules from this chapter and calibrate each one against the too-broad/too-narrow framework, rewriting any that are miscalibrated and documenting your reasoning for the final thresholds chosen.
slots.deliverable: A documented alert-calibration review with final, justified thresholds for each rule.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a real, project-specific pre-launch checklist for your Vault using this lesson's categories (the contract itself, who can touch it after launch, the off-chain stack, and watching it go live), and go through it item by item against your actual project, marking each true/false with evidence.
slots.deliverable: A completed, evidence-backed pre-launch checklist for your own project.

slots.practicalActivity: Browse a real live audit contest board (e.g. Code4rena) and a real bug bounty explorer (e.g. Immunefi), and design a severity/payout table for your own Vault project scaled as a percentage of its (hypothetical) TVL, following the lesson's Critical/High/Medium/Low structure.
slots.deliverable: A designed, severity-tiered bug bounty payout table for your own project.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a real `depositCap` state variable and `require` check to your Vault contract, write a test confirming deposits revert once the cap is reached, and write a one-paragraph policy for what evidence would justify raising it later.
slots.deliverable: A deployed Vault with a tested, enforced deposit cap plus a written cap-raising policy.

slots.practicalActivity: Write your own launch-day runbook for the Vault project, sequencing the before/during/after steps from this lesson against your own actual multisig signers, monitoring dashboard, and communications channel.
slots.deliverable: A complete, project-specific launch-day runbook document.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: run a full mock launch of your Vault project end to end — re-run the pre-launch checklist live, deploy with a deliberately low cap to a fresh testnet, verify on the explorer, and announce only after verification, following your own runbook step by step.
slots.deliverable: A completed mock launch, executed against your own written runbook, with evidence at each step.

slots.practicalActivity: Review: write a short capstone brief tying the whole course together — pick your Vault project and map each of its six chapters' disciplines (testing, CI/CD, deployment, hosting, monitoring, launch) to the specific artifact you built for it, as a portfolio-ready summary.
slots.deliverable: A capstone brief mapping all six chapters' disciplines to real artifacts from your own Vault project, ready for a portfolio.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can take a smart contract from a fuzzed-and-invariant-tested local build through a gated CI/CD pipeline, a multisig-controlled multi-chain testnet deployment, live monitoring and alerting, and a rehearsed mainnet-launch runbook — the complete real-world deployment lifecycle a blockchain engineering team actually follows.
